thread:
maria: Heads up — bringing up a converted Mistral-3B-v2 (converted from official weights) and seeing a weird long-context degradation after ~1.5k tokens. Short interactions look fine, but any prompt >1500 tokens drifts and embeddings at the end look shifted.

maria: Quick repro: conversion pipeline: `convert_weights --src mistral_v2.ckpt --dst gemmaf32 --tokenmap auto` then `quantize --model gemmaf32 --qtype nf4 --group 64`. Ran our standard chat-evals and quality drops after ~1500. Attached trace logs below.

maria: snippet from log showing kv indices mismatch:
```
[kvcache] set key idx=0 for token_id=1
[kvcache] set key idx=1 for token_id=2
...later...
[kvcache] get key idx=0 returned token_id=3
```

arun: :eyes: that kv idx drift looks like token id mapping shifted during conversion. Did `tokenmap auto` remap BOS/EOS or pad differently?

maria: I suspected that. The converter printed a warning about unknown special tokens and said `fallback: offset+1`. Not ideal.

jade: also check rotary params — Mistral uses base 10000 but our gemma runtime expects 8192 scaling for certain head-dims. If rotary base differs, phase alignment over long sequences can cause attention to misroute.

simon: +1 on rotary. But kv index mismatch in logs points to tokenizer mapping first. If token ids shift by +1, kv cache will store under wrong slot and later reads will associate wrong tokens.

gwen: quick check: what are BOS/EOS/pad ids in the converted vocab vs runtime tokenizer?

maria: converted vocab head: BOS=1, EOS=2, PAD=0. Runtime tokenizer: BOS=0, EOS=2, PAD=1. So BOS/PAD swapped.

arun: that explains it — pad id used in runtime becomes BOS in model space causing prefix caching behavior to be off. Simple remap should fix it.

jade: but still run a rotary sanity check after remap. If rotary_base mismatch exists, errors accumulate with length even if tokens are correct. Run: `check_rotary --model converted --expected-base 10000`

maria: trying remap now. Quick hack I used in loader:
```
# loader remap
mapping = {0:1, 1:0}  # swap pad <-> bos
for old,new in mapping.items():
    vocab_ids = [new if vid==old else vid for vid in vocab_ids]
```

maria: also redoing quant with group size 128 per simon's suggestion.

simon: group 64 can exacerbate per-head scale drift in nf4 for this arch. Use group 128 or per-channel quant to compare.

eval-bot: auto-eval summary for "chat-bench-long" (run 2030123457): baseline perplexity@512=6.2, converted@512=6.9; baseline@2048=7.8, converted@2048=14.1. hallucination_rate@2048: baseline=0.03, converted=0.27. Full logs: /evals/2030123457

gwen: wow that's significant. Remap + rotary check + re-quant should reduce that. Can you also run the embedding drift test? `embed-drift --seed 42 --len 2048`

maria: running embed-drift -> initial run shows cosine drop to 0.72 at 1700 tokens (should be >0.95). After remap quick test it jumps to 0.94.

maria: next I'll re-quant with group128 and re-run full eval. Will post results.

deploy-bot: note: model conversion flagged as "blocked for prod" until long-context regression < 10% delta vs baseline. Please open PR with conversion fixes and link to evaluation artifacts.

arun: one more gotcha — check tokenizer normalization differences (NFKC vs none). If conversion used raw bytes->ids and runtime uses normalized text, you can get mismatch in multi-byte tokens at edges.

maria: thanks all — doing remap + rotary check + re-quant now. If that cleans up, will send PR with conversion script changes and unit test for BOS/PAD mapping and a rotary sanity check.

jade: if you want I can add a quick regression test to the quant pipeline that runs the 2048-long embed-drift smoke check so we catch this earlier.

maria: please do. Appreciate the help. Will update thread with results in ~30m.
